newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes under pressure from LATAM.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes under pressure from LATAM.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes remained under pressure from South American imports Friday, as refiners continued to buy foreign barrels for June production, traders said.

Tosco on Thursday bought a 360,000-barrel cargo of Cano Limon from Colombia's state-run Ecopetrol. The cargo will load June 13-23 and will arrive in late June, said traders familiar with company buying practices. They declined to give a price.
Cano Limon, an substitute for West Coast benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, has a gravity of 29.5 degress and 0.47 percent sulfur.
West Coast players waited for Ecopetrol to award two Cusiana cargoes Friday afternoon around 1600 PDT/2000 GMT.
Cusiana, rich with gasoline, is being bid around $1.40-45 under WTI, with offers seen minus $1.20, traders said.
The grade is sold to U.S. Gulf Coast refiners more often than to West Coast players, traders said.
Imports put pressure on most California grades. The widening ANS discount lowered demand for Line 63, a substitute grade which is blended from California crudes.
Buena Vista, a component of 63, dropped 50 cents on the California postings market Thursday. Chevron dropped its postings for Buena from $16.70 to $16.20 a barrel.
Traders reported no deals in Line 63 and heavy California grades.
